title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 113
paragraphs: The fighting at Marathon went on for a long time. In the center of the line, where the Persians themselves and the Sacae were drawn up, the barbarians were winning — here they had broken the Greek ranks and were pursuing them inland. But on both wings, the Athenians and the Plataeans each had the advantage; and being victorious there, they let the routed part of the barbarians flee unmolested, drew the two wings together, and fought the troops who had broken their center. In that fight the Athenians prevailed. They followed the fleeing Persians, cutting them down as they went, until they came to the sea; then they called for fire and began to lay hold of the ships.
